issues.title: Missing nondegeneracy hypothesis in the degree-one minimax comparison

failure_location.quote: As $\Re(\xi_j^{(1)})\ne\Re(\xi_j^{(N)}) $ it is straightforward to show

issues.failure_explanation: In the inherited complex-shift setting, the assumptions permit A=cI with c>α^(1/ℓ). Then ξ_j^(1)=ξ_j^(N)=c−λ_j. The displayed Chebyshev argument divides by ξ_j^(1)−ξ_j^(N), and the quoted proof premise is false. If the degree-one formula is interpreted by cancellation or a limit, both the optimal and Chebyshev polynomials vanish on the singleton spectrum, so the claimed strict comparison also fails. The proof therefore requires a nondegenerate spectral interval.
issues.overall_effect: The proposition does not cover scalar-spectrum SPD matrices as stated. No later formal result relies on this degree-one optimal-polynomial comparison.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend the proposition to assume a nondegenerate spectral interval, for example μ_1>μ_N, equivalently Re(ξ_j^(1))≠Re(ξ_j^(N)), and restrict the strict degree-one comparison to that case. State separately that when μ_1=μ_N the spectrum is a singleton and both degree-one residual polynomials can vanish, so equality rather than strict inequality occurs. No dependent result requires alteration.
issues.why_classification: This is not a typo because the proof uses a missing premise and the strict claim is genuinely false for scalar-spectrum matrices. Nevertheless, a standard one-line nondegeneracy qualification or routine singleton case split preserves the method and the full regular-case conclusion, and the defect has no downstream propagation. That is a minor issue.

issues.title: Incorrect right-hand side in the real saddle-point construction
issues.failure_explanation: Write λ_j=a+ic, x_j=u+iv, b_j=p+iq, and B=A−aI. The complex equation gives Bu+cv=p and Bv−cu=q. Consequently, the displayed saddle matrix applied to (u,−v) has value (−q,p). The old vector (−p,q) therefore specifies a different linear system for a general complex right-hand side.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the saddle-point construction—and hence the specified application of the P_SP preconditioner—solves the wrong block problem for a general right-hand side. The subsequent eigenvalue theorem concerns only the unchanged saddle matrix and is not affected by this right-hand-side error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side of eq:saddlesystem by (-Im(b_j), Re(b_j))^T and use that vector in the stated saddle-point construction. The saddle matrix, unknown vector, block preconditioner, and matrix-eigenvalue theorem remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old complex equation and the explicit decompositions x_j=u+iv and b_j=p+iq uniquely force the correction: the displayed saddle matrix applied to (u,-v)^T equals (-q,p)^T. Thus this is a transcriptional component-order error with one source-determined correction, not a defective argument or algorithmic redesign.

issues.title: Overbroad scope of the matrix–vector-product budget

failure_location.quote: The total permitted number of matrix--vector products with $A$ used to apply any of our new preconditioners is given by $\ell n_x  \resource$, where $\resource$ is a user-defined parameter.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We allocate the same maximum number of inner iterations to all methods, which results in different computational budgets for $\mathcal{P}_{NC}$ and $\mathcal{P}_{SP}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that ℓn_xη is the permitted matrix–vector-product budget for every new preconditioner. The old paper actually establishes that this is the budget for P_NC, while tab:compbud gives P_SP a budget of 2(ℓ−1)n_xη products plus ℓ AMG initializations. Because the paper assumes ℓ>2, these matrix–vector-product counts differ materially; the universal wording understates the P_SP resource requirement.
issues.overall_effect: The sentence misleadingly suggests a common resource cap for the nested Chebyshev and saddle-point methods, although the table and subsequent numerical accounting use distinct costs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the universal budget sentence with method-specific accounting: each application of the nested Chebyshev preconditioner is allotted ℓ n_x η matrix–vector products with A, whereas the saddle-point preconditioner is allotted 2(ℓ−1)n_xη such products plus ℓ AMG initializations, as recorded in tab:compbud. The subsequent numerical accounting can remain unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The common resource cap is a coherent substantive cost claim, so withdrawing it for the saddle-point method is not merely a typo and does not preserve the literal guarantee without loss. However, the correct larger budget is already established locally by the table and subsequent accounting; the algorithms and numerical results need no reconstruction, and a comparable method-specific cost statement survives. This is a limited weakening warranting a moderate classification.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: The total permitted number of matrix--vector products with $A$ used to apply \jt{the nested Chebyshev} preconditioners is given by $\ell n_x  \resource$, where $\resource$ is a user-defined parameter.
